articles.title: US attorney warns Chinese espionage is 'extremely pervasive,' says Beijing 'playing the long game'
articles.summary: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli says Chinese espionage is "extremely pervasive" after his office charged alleged spies in recent months.
articles.body: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said Chinese espionage is "extremely pervasive" in the U.S. following the arrest of an alleged Chinese agent in Los Angeles this month. Essayli told Fox News Digital in an interview that his office has pressed charges against several alleged Chinese spies in recent months, saying Beijing is brazen in its attempts to build their access inside the U.S. "I think it's extremely pervasive," Essayli said of Chinese spying. "China is one of our biggest adversaries, and they're committed to advancing their interests. And they're playing the long game, and so they are willing to put a lot of resources into developing sources, recruiting people within the U.S. to advance their interests. CHINA EXPERT WARNS BEIJING WANTS AMERICANS — NOT THE CCP — TO SPREAD ITS MESSAGE "They're willing to steal our technology; they're willing to engage in espionage here. So, there's no limit to what China is willing to do. It is a huge, huge concern. We have to be vigilant, and we have to disrupt these operations on our soil," Essayli said. "We have to protect our sovereignty." "If you look at just the cases we brought this year, just in my office, I mean, you had cases where the woman from Irvine was engaged in espionage against the Taiwanese president's family member. I had a guy last week we arrested, he sold more than $300 million in SI chips, formerly known as AI chips, to China," he continued. "You had a mayor of a local city that we charged for serving as an unregistered agent of China as well, pushing out their propaganda and taking orders from China." FORMER CALIFORNIA MAYOR ADMITS TO SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING BEIJING PROPAGANDA IN US "So, it's extremely pervasive. It's a huge problem, but the FBI is on it," he said. "They have entire squads dedicated to combating this, and we're committed here at the U.S. Attorney's Office to supporting those investigations and bringing criminal charges to disrupt these operations." Wanying Zhang, 34, of Irvine, was arrested earlier this month for allegedly working with an associate to photograph and record the family outside their Seattle-area home, according to a criminal complaint obtained by Fox News Digital. CHINA-LINKED HACKERS INFILTRATED US GOVERNMENT NETWORKS BEFORE FBI TAKEDOWN Authorities nabbed Zhang, who goes by "Heather" in the U.S., at the Los Angeles airport as she attempted to board a plane to China. Essayli said FBI Los Angeles agents arrested Zhang on a federal charge of acting as an unregistered agent of the People’s Republic of China. CALIFORNIA MAYOR ACCUSED OF SECRETLY WORKING FOR CHINA, SPREADING PROPAGANDA WHILE IN OFFICE: FEDS She allegedly traveled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and sent them photos, videos and license plate information. "She coordinated the trip with an associate and used tradecraft to avoid detection," Essayli wrote. "She never notified the attorney general she was acting for a foreign government, a federal offense." GOOGLE ENGINEER STOLE AI SECRETS FOR CHINA, SENATE HEARS IN EXPLOSIVE TESTIMONY Speaking on "The Big Weekend Show" Sunday, Essayli said Zhang is a naturalized U.S. citizen and confirmed the alleged surveillance targeted a relative of Taiwan’s president. "She was conducting surveillance on behalf of the Chinese government. She was acting as a foreign agent," Essayli said. "And she was spying on a relative of the president of Taiwan here in the U.S." The alleged target was Ting-Yu Lai, the U.S.-based son of Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te, CBS News reported, citing law enforcement sources. The complaint does not name him. "Saw him. Young male. It’s that young one," Zhang allegedly messaged a Chinese government contact while outside the home. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I am video recording," she allegedly added before sending two license plate numbers.

articles.title: Trump aide spars with Loomer over Zelensky
articles.summary: The escalating feud between President Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over a recent diesel deal with Russia has spilled into MAGA circles, sparking a clash between a Trump adviser and far-right activist Laura Loomer over her defense of the Ukrainian leader. Loomer, a staunch supporter of Trump who has informally advised the president in…
articles.body:
The escalating feud between President Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky over a recent diesel deal with Russia has spilled into MAGA circles, sparking a clash between a Trump adviser and far-right activist Laura Loomer over her defense of the Ukrainian leader.

Loomer, a staunch supporter of Trump who has informally advised the president in the past, recalled her July interview with Zelensky in Ukraine, during which he expressed support for Trump.

“When I interviewed President Zelenskyy and he invited me to Mariinsky Palace, he told me he would happily hold elections in Ukraine once [Russian President Vladimir] Putin stopped attacking” Ukraine, she wrote on social media Sunday.

“He had nothing but praise for President Trump and said he is eager to sign a deal to end the war, but that ‘deal’ cannot be unconditional surrender of Ukraine’s sovereignty to Russia,” she continued.

Alex Bruesewitz, a top adviser to Trump whose political consulting firm runs several of the president’s most prominent social media accounts, pushed back on Loomer’s defense of Zelensky and accused him of undermining Trump.

“He called the President ‘weak’ two days ago and bombed oil refineries moments after the President announced a deal with Russia,” Bruesewitz wrote on social media Sunday in response to Loomer’s post. “Let’s stop pretending that he’s a good ally.”

He continued: “If you’re still in communication with him, you should tell him to stop undermining Trump and hurting the American people with his actions.”

Trump suggested Saturday that Ukraine should replace Zelensky with a leader willing to negotiate an end to the Russia-Ukraine war after the Ukrainian president criticized the White House’s decision to lift sanctions on Russian diesel.

“He wants to make problems for the world,” Trump said of Zelensky, blaming him for the surge in diesel prices. “He wants to make problems for our farmers, our ranchers with diesel fuel because Russia supplies a large portion of the diesel fuel throughout the world.”

The dispute also drew in Rep. Dan Crenshaw (R-Texas), who clashed with Bruesewitz after criticizing Tesla CEO Elon Musk’s remarks about Zelensky.

“Why don’t you turn on Starlink over Russia so the Ukrainians can take out Russian ballistic missile launchers?” Crenshaw wrote Sunday in response to Musk , whose post echoed calls for a change in Ukraine’s leadership.

Bruesewitz fired back at Crenshaw, pointing to the Texas Republican’s defeat in this year’s primary against Trump-backed Texas state Rep. Steve Toth (R).

“As an outgoing, backbench member of Congress, please stop trying to obstruct President Trump’s efforts to negotiate a peace deal between Ukraine and Russia,” Bruesewitz wrote on social media Monday.

Crenshaw, a vocal proponent of U.S. military aid to Ukraine, responded with what he called a “free civics lesson.”

“I know the subject of geopolitics is hard for keyboard warriors like yourself, but it turns out that increasing your own leverage and decreasing your opponent’s leverage is what creates the conditions for a peace deal,” Crenshaw wrote on social media Monday.

The exchanges come as Trump faces mounting pressure to curb rising energy costs ahead of the midterm elections.

He received pushback from the Ukrainian leader and Democratic lawmakers over a recent agreement with Putin to funnel millions of tons of Russian diesel to the global marketplace in an effort to address fuel costs.

Zelensky called the agreement a “ birthday gift ” to the Russian leader, warning that it could provide Russia with additional revenue to finance its more than four-year war against Ukraine.

Ukraine subsequently struck a major Russian oil refinery hours after Trump’s announcement of the deal, further escalating tensions over the agreement.

Trump on Sunday declared an energy ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine “effective immediately,” warning the two countries not to break it. On Monday, Zelensky accused Russia of violating the ceasefire by continuing to strike Ukraine’s energy facilities.

articles.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle caught red-handed, must resign
articles.summary: Kimberly Guilfoyle is the current U.S. ambassador to Greece and a longtime cheerleader for President Trump. She is also a former Fox News personality, long-ago ex-wife of Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-Calif.), and, more recently, ex-girlfriend of Donald Trump Jr. And she’s for sale. The Wall Street Journal has the receipts: Guilfoyle promised Eric Deters, a quixotic…
articles.body:
Kimberly Guilfoyle is the current U.S. ambassador to Greece and a longtime cheerleader for President Trump. She is also a former Fox News personality, long-ago ex-wife of Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-Calif.), and, more recently, ex-girlfriend of Donald Trump Jr.

The Wall Street Journal has the receipts : Guilfoyle promised Eric Deters, a quixotic political operative and fundraiser for Republicans, special access to a number of administration officials who might help him with his pet causes, which included a dispute over his taxes with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). In exchange, she wanted $100,000 to help pay off her credit card debt.

“You could just send it here,” she wrote, texting Deters a link to the American Express website. “It won’t show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express that’s all that will show.”

Guilfoyle was keenly aware of the impropriety and repeatedly texted Deters to stop providing written evidence of their dealings and instead just call her up if need be — and to pay the money. “What a nightmare,” she wrote at one point. “You’ll literally cost me my ambassadorship stop writing.”

Deters did not pay off Guilfoyle’s credit card debt, though she did contact IRS Commissioner Billy Long about his case. She also bragged about her access to a host of other top Trump officials: FBI Director Kash Patel, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi, and others. “Every secretary of you know defense, transportation, treasury commerce IRS commissioner everyone gets right back to me,” she told Deters in 2024.

So, first, this is nakedly corrupt, and Guilfoyle should resign as ambassador or be impeached and removed. She cannot be trusted to represent U.S. interests abroad when she has proven that she is willing to peddle influence with the Trump administration in exchange for personal enrichment.

Second, it’s fair to ask some questions about Trump Jr., whose relationship with Guilfoyle ended before she was nominated to be ambassador to Greece. Nevertheless, in her message to the IRS commissioner, she mentions that “Don Jr. and I are very close with Eric Deters.” Trump Jr. subsequently married a model, Bettina Anderson. Their wedding was secretly paid for by Umar Kremlev, a Russian oligarch. (Kremlev has since claimed that Trump Jr. paid him back.)

While the oligarch maintains he had simply struck up a friendship with the couple and wanted to buy them a nice wedding gift, you would have to be very, very gullible not to suspect that his real aim was to influence the administration’s policy toward Russia. It’s possible Trump anticipated this and skipped the wedding for this very reason.

My point is this: Evidence is accumulating that suggests Guilfoyle and Trump Jr. are the kinds of people who will take money in exchange for doing favors. Perhaps unwittingly in Trump Jr.’s case, but obviously quite willfully in Guilfoyle’s. And while they aren’t together anymore, they were a power couple at the center of Trump’s orbit throughout his first term.

This irks me, as someone who cares about hypocrisy. Remember Hunter Biden ? The man who was at the center of countless congressional inquiries over allegations that he was paid by foreign interests in order to lobby his dad, President Biden? Republicans turned this into a huge issue and doggedly pursued it — to be clear, with plenty of justification. I criticized Biden pardoning his son as a clear example of the president abusing his power to thwart a legitimate investigation into his doings.

But look, there’s no way around this: Trump Jr. letting a Russian oligarch pay for his wedding is at least as suspicious as anything Hunter Biden did. And now his ex-girlfriend is caught red-handed engaging in precisely the kind of kickback scheme that birthed the “Biden crime family” moniker? By any reasonable standard, this is just as bad — or significantly worse.

Unfortunately, I suspect many Republicans and conservative commentators will greet these revelations with the exact same stony silence that Democrats opted for when Hunter Biden was under the microscope. I hope I’m wrong, though.

And look, viewers know that I’m not someone who suffers from Trump Derangement Syndrome. I have praised the president for many of his initiatives. I agree with him on the paramount issue of AI and tech. I support his efforts to reduce cumbersome regulation and shrink the federal bureaucracy. I love his Supreme Court picks. I agree that Europe should shoulder more of the burden of their own defense. I think the Democratic Party is about to fall under the influence of outright socialists, who will destroy the country on a foundation level and empower radicals who hate the Constitution, borders, capitalism, prisons, and our very way of life.

But you just can’t govern like this. You can’t let foreign oligarchs or domestic millionaires purchase your vote, and you can’t surround yourself by people who are eager to lobby for quixotic causes in exchange for cold heart cash. This is naked corruption.

It was naked when Hunter Biden did it too. But we can’t be so blinded by our partisan blinkers that we just say, well, it’s my team, it’s better than the alternative. I agree, personally, that it’s better than the alternative. But I also know if I left my “side” get away with murder, there will be a lot of blood on my hands. So I’m calling it out.

If the GOP wants to remain a viable governing coalition — if they want us to get excited for people like, um, Ken Paxton, in Texas — they need to remind us that they are actually better than the other side.

Kimberly Guiloyle, I’m sorry to say, sounds like a real cheap date. I would hope better for Don Jr., but I’m worried! President Trump may actually be more disciplined than these people, but he better get them in line, and fast. Or else we can kiss the midterms good bye, and then we’ll really have to deal with socialism.

Robby Soave is co-host of The Hill’s commentary show “Rising” and a senior editor for Reason Magazine. This column is an edited transcription of his daily commentary.

articles.title: Hillary Clinton recalls viral moment with Obama: ‘I really hope that Donald Trump is watching’
articles.summary: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton over the weekend discussed a viral moment she shared with former President Obama a few months ago at an event after former first lady Michelle Obama noted her husband’s Nobel Peace Prize. “I was at the opening of the Obama library, which I hope you all get to visit,…
articles.body:
Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton over the weekend discussed a viral moment she shared with former President Obama a few months ago at an event after former first lady Michelle Obama noted her husband’s Nobel Peace Prize.

“I was at the opening of the Obama library, which I hope you all get to visit, and, you know, Bill and I were up there with the former presidents and first ladies and sitting behind, you know, Barack and Michelle and their daughters,” Clinton said at a Saturday event for the Nebraska Democratic Party.

“So, when Michelle gave that very touching and clever speech about all the things that her husband had done that the other guy hasn’t, and when she got to, and then, you know, the Nobel Peace Prize, I just burst into laughter,” she added, seemingly referencing President Trump.

During the grand opening of the Obama Presidential Center in June , Michelle Obama noted her husband winning a Nobel Peace Prize during a speech, a line that elicited laughter from Clinton. Former President Obama then turned around and could be heard talking to Clinton, who was sitting behind him.

“I thought it was so perfect. And, so, Barack turns around and he kind of, you know, grins at me, and so I lean forward and I said, ‘I really hope that Donald Trump is watching this, and I really hope he heard that line. And, you know, I think he’s got to feel like he is, you know, in the 10th circle of hell or something because of this litany of everything you’ve done,’ and Barack goes, ‘Yeah, me too. I hope so.’”

Trump has expressed his desire for a Nobel Peace Prize on numerous occasions. Last week, the president asserted that he should have been awarded the prize instead of this year’s winner.

Trump reupped his exaggerated assertion that he has “settled eight Wars” in a Friday evening Truth Social post. He also said that he was “about to settle, or win, two more,” referring to Iran and the Russia-Ukraine war.

“The United States of America, represented by me, as your President, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t,” he wrote.

“This is an indelible stain on Norway, one that will never be forgotten,” Trump continued. “The Nobel ‘Peace’ Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of Radical Ideologues who are Anti-Democracy, and Enemies of Civilization!”

The Hill has reached out to the White House for comment.

articles.title: Federal judge admonishes Trump administration over East Potomac Park tree removal
articles.summary: A federal judge scolded Trump administration lawyers on Monday for failing to provide sufficient notice before cutting down hundreds of trees in East Potomac Park over the weekend, saying she was “beyond disappointed” with the government’s conduct. “I trusted you all not to do precisely what you have done,” U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes said…
articles.body:
A federal judge scolded Trump administration lawyers on Monday for failing to provide sufficient notice before cutting down hundreds of trees in East Potomac Park over the weekend, saying she was “beyond disappointed” with the government’s conduct.

“I trusted you all not to do precisely what you have done,” U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes said during an emergency hearing, adding that the government had lost “all of its credibility” in the case.

Reyes is overseeing a lawsuit brought by the DC Preservation League and two individuals seeking to block an overhaul of the public golf courses on the property, which President Trump has said he wants converted into a championship-caliber course capable of hosting professional tournaments.

East Potomac Park is home to three golf courses, including an 18-hole public facility that offers affordable rates and serves tens of thousands of players every week. It is also a popular biking, running and picnicking location for many Washington, D.C., locals and tourists each year.

The property for the last several years has been operated by the National Links Trust, a local nonprofit that had been charged with maintaining the golf course at East Potomac, along with two other properties at Rock Creek Park and Langston on the District’s northeast side.

The Trump administration’s plans for East Potomac Park have roiled local community activists who contend the government is illegally redeveloping public land at the behest of the president, drawing comparisons to the ballroom he is constructing at the White House and plans for a massive arch across the Potomac River in Arlington.

Workers removed roughly 430 trees from the park on Saturday as part of what officials described as an effort to restore the course to its historic design in line with a 2019 report.

The DC Preservation League sought an emergency temporary restraining order on Sunday, citing “irreversible damage” to the golf course.

“This plan isn’t just about safety,” Kevin Griess, the Superintendent for National Mall and Memorial Parks in the National Park Service (NPS), testified on Monday. “It’s about the restoration of the park to its original historic state of a links golf course.”

Reyes and Abbe Lowell, a lawyer representing the preservation group, pressed NPS officials on why there was a rush to remove the trees if the management plan was finalized seven years ago.

Frank Lands, NPS’s deputy director of operations, testified that there was no “specific urgency,” describing the move as the “normal course of business” consistent with Trump’s executive order to beautify the nation’s capital.

Ahead of the hearing, The judge has barred the National Park Service from conducting any further work on the site until at least 2 p.m. EDT Tuesday while she weighs whether to issue a longer block. She warned of serious consequences if that order is violated.

“I’ve got at least 2-300 more trees that apparently are going to get cut down, and I have no faith that the government isn’t going to cut them down unless there’s an order in place not to do so,” Reyes said.

The Biden-appointed judge told Department of Justice (DOJ) lawyers in May that they must provide notice to the preservation group of any plans to cut down more than 10 trees or perform other maintenance on the site. Dozens of additional trees deemed dead, dying or hazardous had already been removed.

Notice of Saturday’s work came just 12 hours before, the judge said.

“I have given the government the benefit of the doubt and every single time I have been clear that I wanted notice,” Reyes said, later adding that she was “furious” over what happened.

Griess, the superintendent for National Mall and Memorial Parks under NPS, testified under oath that he was not notified of the decision to move forward with tree removal until Oct. 8.

DOJ lawyer Marissa Piropato told the judge that there was “no conscious decision” to withhold information from the court and insisted the department was merely waiting for more details before it submitted its filing.

“None of that is an excuse,” Reyes said.

articles.title: Biden-appointed judge with history of fiery Trump clashes erupts at DOJ: 'You've lost all credibility!'
articles.summary: Judge Ana Reyes screamed at government lawyers over 430 trees cut down at East Potomac Golf Links, demanding answers about late Friday notification.
articles.body: A Biden-appointed federal judge who previously drew a formal misconduct complaint from President Donald Trump's Justice Department for alleged bias erupted at government lawyers again Monday, in a heated showdown over rapid tree removal at a historic golf course on national parkland. Judge Ana Reyes unleashed her latest rebuke during an emergency hearing over hundreds of trees removed from East Potomac Golf Links in Hains Point, D.C. Trump wants to transform the historic public facility into a championship-caliber golf course like his courses in the U.S., Ireland and Scotland – the latest courtroom collision between the administration and its political opponents. Journalist Scott MacFarlane, who live-tweeted from the hearing, described Reyes as "scream[ing]" at administration attorneys over the government's late-Friday notification that tree removal would begin Saturday. A government lawyer acknowledged that approximately 430 trees had already been cut down, according to MacFarlane. OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE TORCHES TRUMP ADMIN IN LATEST COURTROOM SHOWDOWN, REFERS ATTORNEY FOR BAR REVIEW "You've lost credibility!" Reyes told government attorneys, according to MacFarlane's live courtroom reporting. The administration maintains that the removals implement a 2019 National Park Service landscape-restoration plan predating Trump's redesign proposal for the links, which sit on an island connected to the city proper by the Jefferson Memorial and Francis Case Bridge at its western edge. BIDEN-APPOINTED JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP TO RESTORE SLAVERY, CLIMATE CHANGE REFERENCES AT NATIONAL PARKS Reyes, who was born in Uruguay and nominated by Biden in 2023, previously grilled a Trump administration attorney about his religious beliefs during litigation challenging Trump's restrictions on transgender military service — an order she called "biologically inaccurate" according to the Washington Post. The judge questioned how Jesus Christ would respond to "telling a group of people that they are so worthless, so worthless that we’re not going to allow them into homeless shelters?" according to then-DOJ Chief of Staff Chad Mizelle’s complaint. EXCLUSIVE: TRUMP’S DC JUDICIAL NEMESIS TARGETED IN MISCONDUCT COMPLAINT OVER ALLEGED BIDEN DOJ TIES In a 2025 case, Reyes ruled that Trump violated federal notice requirements when he fired several inspectors general but then declined to reinstate them, according to Reuters. Monday's hearing brought another heated exchange, this time over when government lawyers learned of the tree-removal operation and why they waited until the end of the workweek to notify the court. "At 4:55pm on a Friday of a holiday weekend, the plaintiffs and I get [little] notice that hundreds of trees are going to be chopped down," Reyes reportedly fumed at the government, according to MacFarlane. EXCAVATION SET TO BEGIN ON TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 250-FOOT TRIUMPHAL ARCH AMID LEGAL BATTLE When government counsel reportedly acknowledged learning of the operation on Oct. 8 or 9 and said officials were awaiting details, Reyes demanded: "Do you have email or a cell phone?" MacFarlane tweeted that he had never heard a judge "scream at full-voice at a lawyer before," while the UK Independent reported Reyes excoriated federal counsel for about 15 minutes. The uproar comes as preservationists and progressive interests challenge the administration, including former Obama ethics lawyer Norm Eisen — who has engineered a "broad legal resistance" to the president through his group Democracy Defenders Fund, according to its mission statement. Eisen tweeted a victory lap Monday after the court agreed to hear the case in an "emergency’ setting. articles.title: Bill Maher reveals he's having dinner with Trump again, says he was 'really nice' by text
articles.summary: Liberal comedian Bill Maher revealed on his "Club Random" podcast that President Donald Trump invited him back for another White House dinner.
articles.body: Liberal comedian Bill Maher revealed on Monday that he's having dinner with President Donald Trump again. "I'm having dinner with him again next week," Maher told famed Hollywood agent and executive Ari Emanuel during a conversation on Maher's "Club Random" podcast. "After the first dinner, I went back to doing what I do... But then, like, he just, out of the blue, let's have dinner again. And I was like, great. And he was really nice," Maher said. "Like, I promise I won't say bad things about you like I did the last time.' And I texted back, and I said, 'You know what, you're the president of the United States. Say whatever the f--- you want. I'm just glad we're talking.' It's like being called a 'hockey puck' by Don Rickles. It's just what he does. It's how he talks." BILL MAHER REVEALS TRUMP WAS 'GRACIOUS AND MEASURED' AT WHITE HOUSE MEETING, SAYS HE'S NOT THE MAN SEEN ON TV Both Maher and Emanuel agreed it's better to talk with those they disagree with than not. Emanuel, who previously represented Trump when he hosted "The Apprentice," told Maher he had spoken with the president on that Monday. "It blows my mind that there are people in this world and lots of them on the far left who just would turn this opportunity down, a private dinner in the White House with the president, just a few people, say whatever you want," Maher said. "I've heard people say, 'Well, I don't like the war.' Tell him! You can tell them, and I will." Maher took swipes at Emanuel's client Larry David, who previously lambasted the HBO host for his White House dinner last year, while ignoring his agent's relationship with Trump. "It's so interesting to me that Larry David, like, I'm the devil because I talk to him, but his own agent just talked to him on Monday," Maher laughed as Emanuel attempted to avoid weighing in. "You must recognize the hypocrisy there. Somehow, when it's his own agent doing the exact same thing, this is, then we don't play the Hitler card." BILL MAHER FIRES BACK AT LARRY DAVID OVER 'MY DINNER WITH ADOLF' OP-ED, SAYS IT INSULTS '6 MILLION DEAD JEWS' The podcast episode was released Monday but it is unclear whether the dinner has already happened. Neither the White House nor Maher's representatives responded to requests for comment. Maher and Trump had been public foes for more than a decade until their mutual friend Kid Rock brokered a meeting between the two of them, which resulted in a dinner at the White House. He said during a monologue that Trump was more gracious and good-humored than he expected. He also credited Trump for being "much more self-aware than he lets on in public," revealing the subject of the 2020 election came up during his tour of the White House and that he "didn't get mad" about how Maher brought up Trump's rare admission that he had lost. MAHER MOCKS LIBERALS FOR STILL PANICKING ABOUT TRUMP'S ANTICS, PERSONALITY AFTER 10 YEARS "Look, I get it. It doesn't matter who he is at a private dinner with a comedian. It matters who he is on the world stage. I'm just taking as a positive that this person exists. Because everything I've ever not liked about him was, I swear to God, absent at least on this night with this guy," Maher said. "I never felt I had to walk on eggshells around him," he told his audience. "And honestly, I voted for Clinton and Obama, but I would never feel comfortable talking to them the way I was able to talk with Donald Trump. That's just how it went down. Make of it what you will. Me? I feel it's emblematic of why the Democrats are so unpopular these days." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Their relationship appears to be in decent shape behind the scenes despite the public feuding since the dinner. Earlier this year, Maher received the Mark Twain Prize from the Kennedy Center, which Trump oversees as its chairman, and it's been reported that the White House attempted to block Maher from the award. Trump has also repeatedly attacked Maher's "low ratings" on Truth Social in recent months.

articles.title: Obama rolls out ad for Dem Scott Colom in Mississippi Senate race
articles.summary: Former President Obama rolled out a new advertisement this week in support of Democratic Mississippi Senate candidate Scott Colom, amid growing dissatisfaction with the GOP’s handling of key issues among Americans. “Mississippi, it’s time for a change. That’s why you need to send Scott Colom to the U.S. Senate,” Obama said in the ad. “Scott…
articles.body:
Former President Obama rolled out a new advertisement this week in support of Democratic Mississippi Senate candidate Scott Colom, amid growing dissatisfaction with the GOP’s handling of key issues among Americans.

“Mississippi, it’s time for a change. That’s why you need to send Scott Colom to the U.S. Senate,” Obama said in the ad . “Scott is a devoted husband and dad, a seventh-generation Mississippian, guided by his Christian faith.”

“Scott made his community safer, prosecuting violent crimes as district attorney, fighting corruption in Columbus. Now he’s running for Senate to raise wages, lower costs, and save your healthcare and hospitals. Mississippi, your vote matters. Let’s get this done,” he continued.

Colom — a district attorney in Mississippi’s 16th District — is running to unseat incumbent Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith (R), who is running for a second full term in the upper chamber.

Colom was previously nominated twice by former President Biden to serve as U.S. district judge for the Northern District of Mississippi . His nomination was blocked by Hyde-Smith and Sen. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) through the “ blue slip ” tradition.

The Magnolia State is traditionally a red state and has not elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982 , according to 270ToWin, though Republican candidates face a rocky midterm environment .

The Iran war has hit Mississippi especially hard as the prices of gas and fertilizer skyrocketed, partially because of the war.

The average per-gallon price of regular gas in Mississippi is $3.93 as of Monday afternoon, according to AAA , which is up $1.27 from prices a year ago. A gallon of diesel fuel currently costs an average of $5.87 per gallon, which is also up $2.62 from a year ago.

President Trump is currently on a midterm blitz in many red and purple states across the country — such as Texas, Oklahoma and Ohio — to help the GOP’s chances of retaining control of Congress.

Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), a partner of The Hill, gives the Democratic Party a 56 percent chance of regaining control of the Senate. In the state, the DDHQ polling average gives Hyde-Smith a 93 percent chance of keeping her seat.

articles.title: Democrats hammer Trump for late-election raid on Omar’s home
articles.summary: Democrats are up in arms this week after federal agents raided the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.), accusing the Trump administration of weaponizing the government to go after political adversaries. The Democrats are particularly piqued that the operation, conducted Monday morning by agents of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), took place just weeks…
articles.body:
Democrats are up in arms this week after federal agents raided the home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.), accusing the Trump administration of weaponizing the government to go after political adversaries.

The Democrats are particularly piqued that the operation, conducted Monday morning by agents of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), took place just weeks before the Nov. 3 midterms. They’re denouncing President Trump for defying a long-standing Justice Department policy discouraging the escalation of politically sensitive investigations within 60 days of elections.

“As Trump’s popularity craters amid rising prices and his deeply unpopular war, everything he does is an attempt to distract his remaining followers,” Rep. Don Beyer (D-Va.) wrote Monday on social platform X.

“But raiding the home of a member of the opposing party right before the election — and tipping off FoxNews in advance so they are on hand to publicize it — is insanely corrupt even for Donald Trump,” he continued.

In a joint statement, the top three House Democratic leaders — Reps. Hakeem Jeffries (N.Y.), Katherine Clark (Mass.) and Pete Aguilar (Calif.) — characterized the raid as a “deeply disturbing” extension of Trump’s long-running feud with Omar, a foreign-born Muslim congresswoman who is a frequent target of the right.

“For years, Donald Trump and far-right extremists have relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Omar with vile personal attacks and baseless accusations,” the Democratic leaders said in the statement. “Now, less than 30 days until the midterm election, his violent mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family.”

The Democrats, who are favored to win control of the House in November, are vowing to investigate the Omar raid, among other cases they consider to be abuses of executive power, if they have the gavels next year.

“The American people deserve transparency, and we will deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice,” Jeffries, Clark and Aguilar said.

Monday’s raid was conducted before dawn at Omar’s Washington-area home by agents with Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), a criminal unit of ICE. The operation came as the administration has pursued several investigations into Omar across a range of topics, including her finances and immigration status.

HSI, considered an elite unit within ICE, typically investigates major cross-border crime such as human trafficking, child exploitation, and transnational gangs and smuggling.

Though they conducted the search, the Department of Homeland Security referred comment to the Justice Department, which stressed that they got a judicial warrant for the search.

“Today in the Washington, D.C, area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal criminal investigation,” a spokesperson said.

Omar, 44, was born in Somalia but fled the country as a child to escape violence and spent four years in a Kenyan refugee camp before coming to the United States in 1995. She became a U.S. citizen five years later, when she was 17, and was first elected to the House in 2018, becoming one of the first two Muslim women ever elected to Congress.

That background — combined with Omar’s outspoken criticisms of Israel on human rights — has made her a target of conservatives, including Trump, who has questioned her patriotism since her earliest days on Capitol Hill. The president has called Omar “garbage” and has also said Somalis should “go back to where they came from.”

After Monday’s raid, Omar issued a defiant statement accusing Trump of “political intimidation” and saying she “will not be silenced.”

“Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” Omar wrote in a post on X. “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation.”

Last month, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said his office was investigating Omar for potential violations of immigration law stretching back to her arrival in America as a refugee.

“We feel … there may be more to this — the whole family migration and possibly some illegal activity for them to come to the United States to begin with,” Mullin told Benny Johnson , a conservative pundit. “There’s no expiration to that. If we can prove it — that you shouldn’t have been here in the first place — we’ll deport you.”

Mullin also rejected the notion that Omar was being targeted only because she’s a Democrat.

“When we move forward it’s not political. It’s because you chose to break the nation’s laws,” he said. “I don’t make the laws anymore; I’m in charge of enforcing the laws.”

According to Fox News, the basis for the search was part of an investigation into her immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child.

The Justice Department has expanded its investigations into potential fraud in the immigration system, including a denaturalization campaign to strip citizenship of those who did not provide factual information during the process.

But immigration advocates Monday pointed out that the Immigration and Nationality Act already allows immigration judges to issue a waiver to those who were unaware of fraudulent claims made in connection with their application, including if they were a child at the time.

The timing of the search also elicited pushback from Democrats as the Justice Department typically avoids taking major investigative actions like the execution of a warrant within 60 days of an election.

Omar, like her incumbent colleagues running for reelection, is on the ballot in just three weeks.

“Trump has weaponized the @TheJusticeDept , and this is an abuse of power. It is no accident that this raid comes three weeks before an election where Rep. Omar is on the ballot,” Rep. Yvette Clarke (D-N.Y.), chair of the Congressional Black Caucus, wrote on X.

“This is part of the fascist playbook to rile up his supporters in advance of the midterms.”

When Attorney General Todd Blanche was serving as Trump’s personal attorney, he repeatedly argued that any action on that case in the leap up to the contest — even months beforehand — amounted to election interference.

“Trump did not direct the raid on Rep. Omar’s house because there is any reasonable cause. It’s because he thinks his base will turn out for xenophobia and knows they aren’t turning out for his Iran war, price spikes or grift. It’s gross authoritarianism – nothing more,” Rep. Sean Casten (D-Ill.), wrote on X.

Though the search of Omar’s home has not yet resulted in criminal charges, it’s one of several actions the Justice Department has taken against sitting Democratic lawmakers.

Rep. LaMonica McIver (D-N.J.) is facing charges related to a scuffle with law enforcement outside a detention facility, with the Trump administration accusing her of attacking immigration agents with her forearms.

Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, also referred California Democrats Sen. Adam Schiff and former Rep. Eric Swalwell for charges related to allegations of mortgage fraud that both denied.

Rep. Ayanna Pressley (D-Mass.) — who is a member of the group of progressive House members known as the “squad,” alongside Omar — pointed out that those searches and other actions routinely targeted Black women, noting mortgage allegations were also made against New York Attorney General Letitia James (D) and Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook.

“This is a gross abuse of power & the latest in a decade-long, racist smear campaign against a duly elected Black Congresswoman,” Pressley wrote Monday on X.

“Trump is a coward who is weaponizing his DOJ [Department of Justice] to fuel hate & intimidate his opponents with baseless attacks like these, just like he’s doing with Rep. McIver, Lisa Cook, and Tish James.”

articles.title: Danny Trejo says he’s ‘not pro-ICE’ amid backlash over Daily Wire ‘Pawn Shop’ movie
articles.summary: Actor and Los Angeles businessperson Danny Trejo said he does not back Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as he faces backlash for signing on to perform in the film “Pawn Shop,” which is produced by conservative commentator Ben Shapiro’s Daily Wire. Production resumed in Livingston, Mont., on Monday after residents complained about the project’s impact…
articles.body:
Actor and Los Angeles businessperson Danny Trejo said he does not back Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as he faces backlash for signing on to perform in the film “Pawn Shop,” which is produced by conservative commentator Ben Shapiro’s Daily Wire.

Production resumed in Livingston, Mont., on Monday after residents complained about the project’s impact on a nearby food bank and claimed there were improper warnings about the film’s stunts, Variety reported . Shapiro lambasted the initial pause as “content discrimination.”

Trejo, who told TMZ on Friday that he shared with people on the film’s set that he was drawn to playing a positive depiction of a Latino who is a veteran, wrote on Instagram that same day that his job on the film “is to tell a story.”

“I am a proud Mexican who has always been and will always be a supporter of my community. I am also obviously pro-immigrant,” the actor wrote. “I am not pro-ICE. I know where I come from and I know our struggles.”

His son, actor Gilbert Trejo, also addressed the backlash toward his father online. He reiterated that his dad, known for playing knife-wielding villains and anti-heroes like in “Desperado” and “Machete,” respectively, is not “pro-ICE” and he “jumped at the idea of playing a good guy.”

“About two weeks into shooting, everyone, including us, found out Ben Shapiro was involved,” Gilbert Trejo wrote online in a post later shared by local news outlet San Fernando Sun/El Sol . “My 82-year-old dad has never heard of Ben Shapiro, I had to explain to him who that is, and what kind of guy he is.”

Gilbert Trejo added that his dad “can’t badmouth” Shapiro and the film, nor walk off set without facing a lawsuit for breaching his contract.

“It’s f‑‑‑ed up. He’s handcuffed to this stupid project, and swaths of people have instantly turned their back on him without knowing any of the facts,” the “Con Air” star’s son continued. “Ben Shapiro got Mexicans to abandon one of their heroes, got his own name to the top of Google’s searches and made us look like angry fools lacking any nuance. He wins.”

The official description for the film reads: “When a Minneapolis riot forces a young ICE officer to complete a high-stakes arrest alone after his partner is killed, he is hunted through the streets by a furious mob intent on freeing the prisoner and punishing anyone who still upholds the law.”

“Barricaded inside a neighborhood pawn shop with a hard-edged Hispanic veteran and the man’s progressive college-age grandson, ordinary men must choose between the rule of law and the chaos that wants to burn it all down in a modern siege of honor and defiance,” the description continues.

TMZ captured video that appeared to recreate the death of Minneapolis resident and U.S. citizen Renee Good , who was killed by ICE officers after an incident amid growing protests to President Trump’s deportation operations in January.

Danny Trejo has become an institution in Southern California life, opening a small chain of successful restaurants and a coffee shop in parts of Los Angeles. He has also been an advocate for helping people addicted to drugs seek help, for veterans and for working with animal welfare organizations.

articles.title: Fort Hood shooter should be executed '13 times over' — but not on live stream, survivor says
articles.summary: Julia Wilson survived the 2009 Fort Hood massacre and wants Nidal Hasan executed, but she has reservations about livestreaming his death penalty.
articles.body: A survivor of the 2009 Fort Hood massacre says she wishes the mass shooter could be killed one time for every life he took that day – but even she is questioning the military's decision to livestream his death. Nidal Hasan, 56, is scheduled to face execution by firing squad on Dec. 3, 2026, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth announced earlier this month that it will be made available to stream to the public. "Why would people want to see that?" Julia Wilson, a former Defense Department civilian employee who survived the shooting 17 years ago, told Fox News Digital. Wilson wants the mass shooter executed, and, as a victim, she wants to attend his execution and look him in the eye. Hasan, an Army psychiatrist at the time, walked into a soldier readiness center on Nov. 5, 2009, on the Texas Army post and opened fire, killing 13 people and wounding 32 others. Following a military court-martial verdict, Hasan was sentenced to death on Aug. 28, 2013. FORT HOOD SURVIVOR SHOT IN HEAD VOWS TO WATCH TERRORIST FACE HISTORIC FIRING SQUAD On Oct. 2, President Donald Trump approved the death sentence, and days later Hegseth announced it would be by a public firing squad. "Personally, I do want to be there," Wilson told Fox News Digital. "I do want to look him in the eye to let him know, ‘Look, I may have been your victim that day, but I'm not your victim anymore. I survived you. My child survived you, a lot of us survived you. You didn't do as much damage as you thought you were going to.'" "You did what you did," Wilson continued of Hasan's attack. "Too bad we can't kill you 13 times over." But Wilson has reservations about the decision to broadcast Hasan's execution to the public. "I'm kind of shocked that they're going to go so far as to televise it," Wilson said. "I don't really know how to feel about that." She fears broadcasting his death could pose a risk of exposing children to the kind of violence she has spent nearly 17 years trying to forget. "Unfortunately, some children may end up seeing that, that don't need to see something like that," Wilson said. "Seeing my soldiers murdered that day, that was the first time I've ever seen anything like that. And I can never wash it out of my mind." "I don't know why anybody would want to actually see something like that happen." Wilson's concerns echo objections raised by lawmakers on both sides of the aisle. "Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting," Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., posted to X on Thursday. "Public executions are what oppressive dictatorships like Iran and Afghanistan do. It should not be happening in America." TEXAS EXECUTES JAMAAL HOWARD DESPITE CONCERNS OVER LETHAL INJECTION DRUG USED IN FAILED TENNESSEE EXECUTION Trump said Saturday that he will make the decision of whether or not to livestream Hasan’s execution, acknowledging that he knows "what the military would like to do" following Hegseth’s confirmation. Vice President J.D. Vance also said Friday that he was not sure that the federal government will be livestreaming the execution, also adding that he would not personally view the livestream. "As far as the execution, I have a lot of mixed feelings on it, to be quite honest," Wilson said. "Yes, I'm glad that it's moving forward. No, I…don't ever want to see another human being die." "But in the same fold, an eye for an eye." Wilson was working at Fort Hood's Soldier Readiness Processing Center when Hasan opened fire. At the time, she was nine months pregnant and had reached her due date. She recalled the moment when she first saw soldiers down and heard the gunfire after pulling into the parking lot upon returning to the center from a lunch break with her mom. "Before I got the chance to shut off my engine and really get out of the vehicle, that's when the gunfire started," Wilson said. "I had several things go through my mind. You know, they say that you have fight, flight or freeze. I kind of had all three. " She recounted the chaos during the shooting after going into the center building for the first time since taking cover in her car, which she says her supervisor advised her to do. "Eventually he came back for me and I figured, ‘Okay, maybe… I'm a little bit out of the chaos.’ No, absolutely not," Wilson said. THREE DEATH ROW INMATES EXECUTED BY LETHAL INJECTION IN RARE SAME-DAY STRING ACROSS US She continued, "I get into my building. Desks are tossed everywhere. It's a total wreck. There's blood on the wall, blood on the floor, people working on people. And I just kind of locked up." "A wounded soldier came in the door opposite of me and said, ‘He's in the building, he’s shooting, get the f–– out of here." Wilson said that Hasan receiving the death penalty will still not bring full justice to the victims of the tragedy. She called out the federal government for classifying the shooting as "workplace violence," urging the shooting to be reclassified as an act of domestic terrorism. "We've been betrayed by the government for 17 years," Wilson said. "They left this as workplace violence. They never declared it domestic terrorism because it was all about, ‘Hey, we need to be politically correct and watch out for his rights.’ Well, what about my rights? And what about me? And what about my family? And what about those that were murdered? And what about those that were injured?" Wilson has written a letter to Trump calling for the reclassification of the shooting to be recognized as domestic terrorism. articles.title: Trump set to rally in Georgia to support Collins in Senate race

articles.body:
( NewsNation ) – President Trump will travel to Georgia on Friday to campaign for Republican Senate candidate Rep. Mike Collins, NewsNation has learned.

The Republican National Committee confirmed the president will travel to Georgia on Oct. 16 for a rally at the Dalton Municipal Airport in Whitfield County. This comes as recent polling shows Collins is fighting an uphill battle to unseat Democratic Sen. Jon Ossoff in Georgia.

Decision Desk HQ polling data shows Ossoff leading 52 percent to 43 percent with less than a month until November’s midterm elections. Georgia is considered a must-win for Democrats in their quest to regain control of the Senate.

Ossoff, the only Democratic incumbent running for a Senate seat in a state Trump won in 2024, debated Collins last week. Both candidates used their allotted time to criticize each other’s family backgrounds and argue that their opponent was not fit to represent Georgia on Capitol Hill.

The president will also campaign for Republican gubernatorial nominee Rick Jackson, who is facing Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, the former mayor of Atlanta. Jackson is leading that race 49 percent to 47 percent, according to DDHQ polling data .

Trump will also reportedly travel to Ohio and Montana this week as part of his red-state campaign push ahead of the midterms.

NewsNation’s Mills Hayes contributed to this report.

articles.title: Judge tears into Trump administration for felling trees on D.C. golf course the president wants to remake
articles.summary: “I’m furious,” U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes told a Justice Department lawyer. “I trusted you all not to do precisely what you have done.”
articles.body: A federal judge on Monday ripped the Trump administration for “inexcusable” gamesmanship after it removed hundreds of trees from a public golf course that the president said he wants to turn into “one of the greatest golf courses anywhere in the world” — a renovation plan being challenged in court. U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes said lawyers for the government had assured her the administration would give her ample warning if it planned any “irreversible” actions at East Potomac Golf Links, only to chop down over 400 trees on the course over the weekend without proper notice. “I’m furious,” Reyes told attorneys from the Justice Department. “I was hearing from everyone on plaintiffs’ side this was going to happen. I said repeatedly, ‘No, I trust the government.’ I trusted you all not to do precisely what you have done,” the judge said. She called the government’s actions “inexcusable.” “What has happened has cost the government all of its credibility,” Reyes added. An attorney for the government, Marissa Piropato, said it gave notice in a court filing shortly before 5 p.m. on Friday, the beginning of the three-day holiday weekend. The work began the next morning, with 430 trees being removed. Piropato told the judge “we did our best” to notify the court and the plaintiff in the case, the DC Preservation League. “You did not do your best. You did your absolute worst,” the judge snapped. The judge issued an order early Monday temporarily barring any other trees from being removed until at least Tuesday, and called an emergency hearing with just hours’ notice, despite it being a federal court holiday. Reyes had previously made clear she did not want to issue a restraining order in the case — “I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees. I am a judge,” she proclaimed at a hearing last month — but said the government’s actions had left her no choice. She called in two officials from the National Park Service to testify virtually about the speed of the government’s actions. Both said the plan came together in the last week, and one, Deputy Director for Operations Frank Lands, said he’d been directed to begin executing it by Greg Wischer, deputy chief of staff to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum. “Yes, a week is fast,” Lands said. “And I’m proud of the fact that we were able to move so quickly.” Reyes ordered Wischer to testify at the hearing, but attorneys said they were unable to immediately find him. The judge ordered him to appear Tuesday and kept the restraining order in place until then. The other official who testified, Superintendent of National Mall and Memorial Parks Kevin Griess, said workers had identified about 300 more trees that still need to be cut down. The judge said at the end of the hearing that she felt she’d been lied to by the government. She noted that the officials said the plan had essentially been greenlighted on Oct. 5, and that the NPS comptroller filed a sworn document in court the next day saying the agency has “no intent to commence significant rehabilitation work until all applicable compliance requirements have been satisfied.” The plaintiffs in the case filed suit earlier this year, following reports President Donald Trump planned to transform the 100-year-old greens into a championship-style course. The plaintiffs said they were concerned the administration would begin renovations without following proper procedures, citing in part the administration’s abrupt razing of the White House’s East Wing last year. Debris from that demolition was later dumped on the course and used as landfill. Trump confirmed his plans for the site in a post on Truth Social in June, calling the current course “dilapidated, worn out, and very dangerous and outdated.” He said that “we have determined that this location can bring tremendous success and prestige back to Washington, D.C.,” and that work “on the new Course, which will go quickly, will begin on September 1st.” At the time, Reyes did not sign a restraining order but told the government to provide her and the plaintiffs’ attorneys “enough notice before some major thing happens” so it could be reviewed first, according to court filings. The government agreed. The plaintiffs said they received notice of this weekend’s massive tree removal about 12 hours before it happened, and that the government represented it as “maintenance activities” unrelated to Trump’s plans. In a filing, the DOJ said the Interior Department was merely implementing recommendations from a 2019 “Cultural Landscape Report,” which was aimed at restoring the course closer to its original design. The plaintiffs said in a court filing Sunday that Trump’s plan for the site would “require massive tree-clearing.” “Defendants would have this Court believe that this unprecedented operation is merely the sudden and purely coincidental fulfillment of recommendations posited in a Cultural Landscape Report seven years ago and is totally unrelated to the ongoing implementation of the Washington National plan,” they wrote. “Even if Defendants were entitled to the benefit of the doubt, they are not entitled to a suspension of disbelief.” Reyes, who was nominated to the bench by President Joe Biden, stressed that she wasn’t happy about having to issue the restraining order, saying, “I don’t think courts should be playing parks and rec.” White House adviser Stephen Miller suggested in a post on X that the judge should stay out of it. “I missed the part of the Constitutional Convention that put federal judges in charge of golf course maintenance,” he wrote.

articles.title: Johnson: Video of Hasan execution could be ‘recruiting tool for future terrorists’
articles.summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said the Pentagon’s plan to livestream the execution of former Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan could be used by terrorist groups to recruit more people, joining a growing list of Republicans who have expressed reservations about broadcasting it publicly. “There are colleagues that have concerns,” Johnson said in an interview…
articles.body:
House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said the Pentagon’s plan to livestream the execution of former Army Maj. Nidal Malik Hasan could be used by terrorist groups to recruit more people, joining a growing list of Republicans who have expressed reservations about broadcasting it publicly.

“There are colleagues that have concerns,” Johnson said in an interview with CBS News. “The concern would be that you would create a video that would be a recruiting tool for future terrorists. We got to think through the policy implications of all that.”

Johnson said he would not watch the livestream if it were to air, and he added that he had not had a chance to speak with President Trump, Vice President Vance or Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth about the matter.

“My role as the leader of the legislative branch is to share my opinion,” he said. “It’s outside of my lane, of course, but I need to tell the White House what some of my colleagues think about that, and not everybody’s in favor of the idea.”

Johnson is the latest high-ranking Republican to question Hegseth’s surprise plan to publicly broadcast the firing squad execution of Hasan, who was convicted and sentenced to death after admitting to killing 13 people in a 2009 shooting at Fort Hood, Texas.

While many Republicans back the death penalty for Hasan, outrage was shared from both sides of the aisle over the plan to livestream the military’s first execution in more than six decades.

Senior lawmakers shared bipartisan condemnation over the livestream, likening it to a dishonorable public spectacle that could embolden terrorism.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) urged Hegseth to reverse course on the decision, warning that it would bring notoriety to Hasan and fulfill his wish of becoming a martyr.

“There is no need to livestream any execution, including this one,” she said on the social platform X. “I would expect this from terrorists and dictators, but not here in America.”

Sen. Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), a vocal critic of Hegseth’s leadership at the Pentagon, called the plan “ beyond disgusting ,” likening it to executions performed in U.S. adversarial countries and oppressive dictatorships.

“Hasan should face the death penalty, but making his execution public and streaming it? Beyond disgusting,” he wrote on X .

Hegseth announced last week that Hasan’s execution by firing squad, scheduled for Dec. 3 in Texas, would be open to the public.

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public,” Hegseth said in an interview with conservative TV outlet Real America’s Voice on Oct. 8.

While Trump did approve Hasan’s execution, the commander in chief said he will make the ultimate decision on whether it will be broadcast to the public.

articles.title: Elon Musk spends $366m to bolster Republican Party in US midterm elections
articles.summary: The barrage of spending comes as Republicans fight to overcome Trump’s slipping popularity and cost of living concerns.
articles.body:
Elon Musk, the trillionaire tech mogul and backer of far-right causes , has reportedly spent $366m since last year to buoy the Republican Party in the United States midterm elections.

The New York Times first reported on Monday that Musk has spent $276m since July alone, including $158m for a super PAC focused on Republican Senate candidates, making him the largest single donor this year.

Musk is considered a close ally of President Donald Trump , the leader of the Republican Party, and was a special government adviser to the White House last year.

Musk’s political action committee, America PAC, has confirmed the spending totals. In a statement to The New York Times, a spokesperson framed the record amount as necessary to defend Congress from a Democratic takeover during the midterm races.

“These robust investments have allowed the GOP apparatus to get its message out so Republicans can have a fighting chance to defy history,” America PAC spokesman Andrew Romeo told the Times.

The barrage of spending by Musk comes as Republican candidates are fighting to overcome Trump’s low popularity and rising concerns about the cost of living among US voters.

Democrats are hoping to capitalise on voter dissatisfaction with Trump’s tenure to seize control of Congress, where Republicans currently hold majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate.

The influence of wealthy donors and PACs has long been the subject of criticism. Opponents argue that such spending distorts US politics in favour of powerful interests .

Musk became the world’s first trillionaire in June, when his aerospace company SpaceX made its initial public offering (IPO) on the Nasdaq stock exchange.

The tech entrepreneur had previously said that he planned to step back from his involvement in US politics, stating in May that he had “done enough” and did not have plans for large spending efforts.

Still, Musk has leveraged his tech holdings and wealth to support right-wing groups around the world.

Last year, for instance, politicians in Germany accused Musk of trying to meddle in the national election. Musk has been a vocal backer of the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which has been accused of adopting a discriminatory stance on immigration and other issues.

Voters in the US will head to the polls on November 3 to cast their ballots in the midterms, which will decide key state and local races, as well as congressional majorities.

The Republican Party is considered to have a sizeable financial advantage over the Democrats ahead of the race, with heavy spending from groups such as MAGA Inc, a pro-Trump super PAC named for the president’s “Make America Great Again” movement.

As of August, MAGA Inc reportedly had $416m in its coffers. The tracking site AdImpact found that it had spent $22m over the past month alone on the tight race unfolding for the open Senate seat in Texas.

Trump has also increased his campaign activities, hosting a string of rallies in the final weeks before the election to help Republicans push their message .

But Democrats appear confident that the Republicans’ spending advantage will not be enough to counter the effects of growing dissatisfaction with Trump.

“Republicans are hoping to buy these elections, injecting tens of millions into races to try and outrun their unpopular candidates, unpopular president and unpopular economy,” said Lauren French, a spokesperson for Democrats’ Senate Majority PAC.

articles.title: Pennsylvania reports sixth measles death
articles.summary: Pennsylvania authorities on Monday confirmed the state’s sixth death connected to a measles case as the state deals with the highest number of cases nationally. The coroner’s office…
articles.body:
Pennsylvania authorities on Monday confirmed the state’s sixth death connected to a measles case as the state deals with the highest number of cases nationally.

The Franklin County Coroner released an advisory on Monday stating a 39-year-old woman with “several underlying conditions” died following a recent measles diagnosis that had been treated. The coroner’s office investigated the death Saturday.

“This is the first death in Franklin County in many years with a patient with a recent history of a measles diagnosis and meets the definition set forth by the Pennsylvania Department of Health for a measles-associated death,” the coroner said.

Pennsylvania’s statewide tally, updated weekly, does not yet reflect this most recent measles-related death due to Monday being a federal holiday. The state dashboard will be updated Wednesday.

The state has the highest number of measles cases and deaths nationally, surpassing 1,000 total infections last week. This year has marked the worst the U.S. has seen in terms of measles transmission in decades, with more than 4,000 cases confirmed so far.

Despite Pennsylvania now reporting six measles-related deaths, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has recorded only two so far, due to the Trump administration changing how measles deaths are counted.

When the first measles-related deaths were reported by the state earlier this year, and local jurisdictions reported not having knowledge of them, federal officials questioned whether anyone died.

In September, the CDC announced it was switching from using the Nationally Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System, a program through which local jurisdictions provide case information in real-time, to using the National Center for Health Statistics, which is more comprehensive in terms of data but, as a result, lags between when a death occurs and the availability of cause of death.

articles.title: Selma Blair taken into custody, hospitalized after allegedly trying to open plane door
articles.summary: Airline officials asked for medical staff to be at the gate when the flight landed to address the injured parties.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Selma Blair was arrested following an airline incident over the weekend, according to authorities.

The “Cruel Intentions” actress was on a Delta Air Lines flight headed to John F. Kennedy International Airport from LAX on Sunday when she reportedly tried to open the plane door midair, resulting in her allegedly punching one flight attendant and biting another after they tried to intervene, TMZ first reported .

The outlet obtained dispatch audio, where airline officials asked for medical staff to be at the gate when the flight landed to address the injuries, including bite marks and a bloody nose.

According to the audio, an unruly passenger bashed her head against a physical partition that separates the different sections of the plane.

One flight attendant was taken to the hospital, the New York Port Authority told NewsNation.

“Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first,” the airline said in a statement.

Blair was detained and transported to a hospital for assessment. The FBI is investigating the alleged in-flight incident.

“Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition,” Blair’s representative told NewsNation in a statement.

Blair, 54, was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis, or MS, in 2018. The disease, which impacts the central nervous system, can affect people differently, but is capable of causing memory difficulties, mobility issues, mood changes, and vision impairment, according to the National Multiple Sclerosis Society .

She revealed in 2021 that she had entered remission. In an April 2026 update to TODAY , Blair said she was “feeling well” and had been relapse-free.

Blair was removed from a flight in 2016 after she said she experienced “a total psychotic blackout” while traveling with her son, who was 4 at the time, Nexstar’s KTLA reports . She explained that it was “a big mistake” after mixing alcohol with medication.

articles.title: Pro-Collins ads target wrong Portland in GOP super PAC mix-up
articles.summary: Ads promoting Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) appeared to target the wrong city of Portland in a Republican super PAC mix-up, running the advertisements in Oregon instead of Maine. “During a recent independent expenditure, our media vendor mistakenly placed approximately $25,000 in digital advertising in the Portland, Oregon media market instead of Portland, Maine,” a spokesperson…
articles.body:
Ads promoting Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) appeared to target the wrong city of Portland in a Republican super PAC mix-up, running the advertisements in Oregon instead of Maine.

“During a recent independent expenditure, our media vendor mistakenly placed approximately $25,000 in digital advertising in the Portland, Oregon media market instead of Portland, Maine,” a spokesperson for Republican Main Street Partnership (RMSP), the nonprofit affiliated with GOP super PAC Defending Main Street, told The Hill.

“The error was identified, the ads were immediately stopped and corrected, and the vendor is refunding Defending Main Street the full amount of the misplaced spend,” the spokesperson said. “No donor funds will be lost as a result of the vendor’s error.”

The mix-up was first reported by NBC News , which identified a Portland, Oregon, resident writing on social media Sunday that she received “5 anti-Troy Jackson ads in the last 24 hours.”

According to Google Ads Transparency Center , the advertisements ran for four days and targeted various zip codes around the Portland, Oregon, area. Before the ad was taken down, it was shown more than 1 million times to people across all demographics in Oregon.

An RMSP spokesperson also directed The Hill to statements from Sarah Chamberlain, the president and CEO of RMSP. In the statements to NBC News, Chamberlain said she was “absolutely furious” that the ad buyer, Cross Screen Media, made such a “ridiculous” error.

“It has nothing to do with us. I would never run an ad in Portland, Oregon, for Susan Collins, for Christ’s sake,” Chamberlain said.

Cross Screen Media released a statement Monday, saying that it was “100% our mistake,” adding that they have refunded the $25,909.61 to the super PAC and began running the ads in Portland, Maine.

Collins is running to defend her seat in the upper chamber for a sixth term against Democrat Troy Jackson, the former president of Maine’s state Senate. The pair faced off in a debate last week that focused on the impact Trump administration tariffs against Canada were having on Maine residents.

Decision Desk HQ, a partner of The Hill, gives Jackson a 54 percent chance of flipping the seat.

articles.body:
Musk gives GOP a boost ahead of the midterms

Tech trillionaire Elon Musk gave $276 million to several Republican super PACs and organizations over the past three months, as the GOP faces headwinds ahead of the midterm elections.

© Jacquelyn Martin, The Associated Press

This brings the Tesla and SpaceX CEO’s total contributions so far to $366 million . A spokesperson for Musk’s America PAC confirmed the numbers to The Hill, which were first reported by The New York Times.

Between July and September, Musk gave $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, a super PAC backing Republican Senate candidates, and $20 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, which supports GOP House candidates.

The move signals Musk’s appetite for political involvement, despite his suggestions he could pull back spending for the midterms.

Musk’s America PAC, which he launched during the 2024 election, received more than $76 million .

He also gave $10 million to the Lone Star Liberty PAC backing Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton, $10 million to the Republican Governors Association and $2 million to the Republican Attorneys General Association.

Musk, who long stayed out of politics, jumped into the political world during the 2024 elections, pouring hundreds of millions into the presidential race for Trump.

He joined the then-candidate on the campaign trail and later led Trump’s cost-cutting effort known as the Department of Government Efficiency . The project sparked controversy for its sweeping job and funding cuts across the federal government.

He departed the White House in late May 2025 and, after a public fallout with Trump, stayed quiet for months in the political space.

Musk said last May he planned to spend “a lot less” on politics, and he later told The Economist in a July interview he “got carried away” and “a little too involved in politics.”

articles.title: Analysis: Trump's global headaches worsen weeks before midterms
articles.summary: As election day looms, the president turns his eyes overseas for help with a pressing domestic problem.
articles.body:
With elections that will decide control of Congress just weeks away and American voters already casting ballots in some battlegrounds, President Donald Trump has turned his eyes overseas – and to Russia, in particular - for help tackling one of his most pressing problems.

World affairs seldom provide easy answers, however, and developments elsewhere have threatened to undermine his efforts to bring down fuel prices before they provide any political benefit.

A whirlwind weekend started on Friday afternoon, as Trump announced a new deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin that would provide the US with hundreds of millions of tons of Russian diesel fuel in the coming months.

High energy prices, particularly for midwestern agricultural states that rely on diesel to power farm machinery and carry their goods to market, have been a growing source of frustration for American voters.

Polls suggest they view the Iran War as the leading cause for their woes, and overall support for Trump, and approval of his handling of the war and the US economy in particular, has dropped precipitously.

Trump heralded his Russian deal in a Truth Social post as bringing "lower prices for Americans," while he ordered his Treasury Department to suspend US restrictions that prevented Russian diesel from being sold on global markets.

Two days later, Trump was back on his social media website, touting a new energy ceasefire agreement between Russia and Ukraine.

The truth, however, was more complicated.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he had no advanced notice of the agreement, although he said his nation would abide by it. Russia, for its part, was silent. And on Sunday night, it launched a new wave of attacks on Ukrainian power plants.

"It's clear that Putin does not read Truth Social," Zelensky noted wryly on Monday. He added: "This winter, if Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire, we will respond."

Trump and Zelensky have had a tumultuous relationship throughout his second term. The American president alternates between blaming Russia and Ukraine for the continuing conflict he previously said would be easy to end once he returned to the White House.

In recent days, Zelensky has been the primary target of Trump's ire, as Ukraine's strikes on Russian oil infrastructure have contributed to worldwide energy shortages.

On Saturday, Trump told reporters at the White House that it was time for Ukraine to get a new president. And both the Financial Times and CNN have reported that the US has threatened to cut off arms sales and intelligence sharing with Ukraine if Zelensky does not halt attacks on Russian refineries. Zelensky "better damn well stop," Trump said.

"I think that the president has a decade long public record of lashing out of people who aren't doing what he wants, when and how he wants to do it," Terry Haines, founder of independent think-tank Pangaea Policy, told the BBC.

It now appears Trump's celebration of the "energy truce" may have been a familiar move for this president, touting an agreement before it had been sealed and delivered. In the past, for instance, he has prematurely announced Middle East ceasefires and sweeping peace agreements.

Whether it is impatience on the president's part with the slow pace of diplomacy or a savvy negotiating tactic to push a deal across the finish line, the result has been to set off a scramble as the world decides what it means – and how to react.

Those reactions didn't take long to arrive.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who has become a vocal critic of the president's on the international stage, offered "strong support" for the energy ceasefire, but condemned the diesel deal as undermining peace and stability in Europe and helping Russia to finance its "illegal, unjustifiable war against Ukraine".

In the US, Trump's diesel announcement prompted similar concern, even among members of his own party. Four Republican senators joined with Democrats in a letter calling on the president to "immediately reverse course".

"Congress explicitly banned Russian energy imports in 2022 to prevent American dollars from financing Putin's brutal war against Ukraine," the senators wrote in a statement released on Sunday. "President Trump's decision to allow Russian diesel imports to the US runs directly counter to that law."
